certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Product Specification. Manufacturers are highly encouraged to apply for a BIS 'Standard Mark' (ISI Mark) as a certified assurance of waterproof barrier quality. Compliance with IS 1398 is widely integrated into defense packaging, seaworthy textile bales, export shipping specifications, and civil construction (such as under-layment beneath concrete linings to prevent moisture loss).

requirements.detail: Specifies Type 1 packing paper as a water-proof, bitumen-laminated kraft paper combination designed for high barrier performance in general packaging.
Under active Amendment No. 1 (August 2004), the wording on Page 4, clause 2.1, line 5 is amended to substitute 'kraft paper' in place of the typographical error 'draft paper'.
Under active Amendment No. 1 (August 2004), the packaging requirements on Page 5, clause 3.4, line 1 are amended to substitute 'length of minimum 100 metres' in place of 'length of 100 metres'.

The laminate must utilize a continuous, uniform interlayer of food-grade or packing-grade bitumen to bond the paper plies. It must present no delamination, bare patches, or bleeding under normal storage temperatures.
The paper must withstand water penetration tests, ensuring that no liquid water seeps through the bitumen barrier when tested under a standard hydrostatic or surface-contact time-exposure head.
Observed or calculated values during testing must be rounded off mathematically in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained must match the specified limit.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 1398 : 1982 is the national Indian Standard specification establishing technical requirements and barrier tests for water-proof, bitumen-laminated packing paper. Formulated by the CHD 16 Sectional Committee, this standard regulates paper comprising multiple plies of kraft paper conjoined by a uniform layer of bitumen to act as an impervious moisture barrier. Active updates, such as Amendment No. 1 (August 2004), correct typographical errors (substituting 'kraft paper' for 'draft paper') and modify packaging rules to mandate a minimum roll length of 100 metres, ensuring durable and secure moisture protection for industrial wrapping, seaworthy bales, and concrete underlays nationwide.
